trajectory_summary: This call starts flat and stays procedurally on-track: the rep runs through address, shading, ownership, interest, bill amount, utility, and credit qualifier in under three minutes, then spends the back half wrestling a bill-photo capture that eventually succeeds. The energy is mostly stagnant rather than built — the customer's one real engagement spike (regret about not going solar two years ago, and later noticing his own usage spike) is acknowledged but not leveraged into a stronger booking push, and the appointment that results is explicitly tentative pending the customer's work schedule.
outcome_dispute: The appointment is not firmly booked — the customer says 'I'll have to look at my work schedule' (07:46) and the rep herself frames it as tentative: 'we'll tentatively schedule you for Monday at 03:30' (10:14). This should be tagged tentative/callback, not a clean booked outcome, since no firm handshake ('is that fair?') or reconfirmed lock occurred.

observed_outcome.quote: Let's tentatively plan for Monday, you said, at 03:30?
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day and time (Monday 03:30) is named, but the customer conditions it on checking his work schedule and both parties use 'tentatively,' with the rep planning a Monday-morning reconfirm call rather than a locked commitment.

Okay.' and 'We can definitely get that lower for you' (02:33) but never turns the number into an explicit reason-to-act framing tied to the appointment; the flip should have landed here or when usage doubling was raised again at 09:52.

primary_coaching_focus.quote: We'll tentatively schedule you for Monday at 03:30. And, again, you've got my info, so if things change, just let me know.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The appointment never gets a firm lock — no hour-block, no computer/no-driving instruction, no 'is that fair?' — leaving a real booking dependent entirely on a Monday-morning reconfirm call. This is the single highest-leverage fix since it directly affects show rate on an otherwise well-run call.

key_moments.quote: I talked to somebody, like, maybe two years ago, and I just kinda regret not doing it then, now.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior solar conversation from roughly two years ago but the rep never asks which company, what was shown, or why it didn't move forward. This is competitive intel the closer would want walking in.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. So the the big federal tax credits, those did end up going away.
key_moments.stewart_read: The schema's required disclosure language is specific: the credit can't be guaranteed on purchased systems, may still apply if installed before year-end, and purchase options exist without it. The rep's line is looser and omits the purchase-options-without-credit clarification entirely.

key_moments.quote: Our electric bill's somewhere between last year, it was, like, $2.90. Now it's, like, $3.53 90. So, like, edging up on 400.
